title: Speech recognition and speech synthesis
learningObjective: Identify features and capabilities of speech recognition (speech to text) and speech synthesis (text to speech).
foundation: Speech recognition (speech to text) turns spoken audio into written text: captions, transcripts, voice commands.
Speech synthesis (text to speech) turns text into natural-sounding spoken audio: reading answers aloud, audiobooks, phone menus.
Azure Speech in Foundry Tools does both, plus translation of speech and more. Multimodal models can also listen and speak directly.
engineer: Speech to text modes: real-time (streaming, for captions and voice assistants), fast transcription (quick synchronous file transcription), batch transcription (large volumes of stored audio, asynchronous). Features: automatic punctuation, language identification, speaker diarization (who spoke when), word-level timestamps, profanity filtering, phrase lists, and custom speech models trained with your audio and text for domain vocabulary and accents.

Text to speech: neural and HD voices in many languages and styles; SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) controls pronunciation, pauses, rate, pitch, volume and speaking style; custom voice (with approval) for a brand voice; text-to-speech avatars.

Other speech capabilities: speech translation (speech to text or speech in other languages), pronunciation assessment (accuracy, fluency, prosody for language learning), keyword recognition, and Voice Live for low-latency voice agents.
Responsible use: custom neural voice and some features require an application and approval; disclose synthetic voices.

example.title: A pharmacy call line
body: Calls are transcribed in real time with a custom speech model that knows drug names; diarization separates pharmacist and caller; batch transcription processes archived calls overnight.
The automated line answers in a neural voice; SSML spells out prescription numbers digit by digit and adds pauses.

configuration.python:
# pip install azure-cognitiveservices-speech azure-ai-textanalytics
import os
import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk
from azure.ai.textanalytics import TextAnalyticsClient
from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential

speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(subscription=os.environ["SPEECH_KEY"], endpoint=os.environ["ENDPOINT"])
speech_config.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"
recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(speech_config=speech_config,
                                        audio_config=speechsdk.audio.AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True))
result = recognizer.recognize_once_async().get()
if result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizedSpeech:
    text = result.text
    language = TextAnalyticsClient(os.environ["ENDPOINT"], AzureKeyCredential(os.environ["SPEECH_KEY"]))
    sentiment = language.analyze_sentiment([text])[0]
    print(text, "->", sentiment.sentiment, sentiment.confidence_scores)

    speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural"
    speechsdk.SpeechSynthesizer(speech_config=speech_config).speak_text_async(f"You sounded {sentiment.sentiment}.").get()
else:
    print("No speech recognized:", result.reason)

troubleshooting.cause: General model doesn't know the vocabulary.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a phrase list or train custom speech.

troubleshooting.symptom: Synthesised voice reads '2025' as a number, not a year.
troubleshooting.fix: Use SSML say-as for dates or numbers.

comparisons.difference: Speech to text reads audio; OCR reads text in images.
Batch processes stored files asynchronously; real-time streams live audio.

misconceptions.reality: Neural and HD voices are natural and expressive.

misconceptions.myth: Speaker diarization identifies people by name.
misconceptions.reality: It separates speakers (Speaker 1, 2); identification needs extra steps.

architectureDecisions: Add custom speech for specialist vocabulary.
